discovery: Quantum simulation of Hubbard models with ultracold atoms in optical lattices, from the superfluid-Mott insulator transition to single-site quantum gas microscopy

nominees.name: Peter Zoller
nominees.affiliation: University of Innsbruck and IQOQI, Austrian Academy of Sciences

nominees.name: Immanuel Bloch
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics and Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / ultracold quantum gases
motivation: Zoller and collaborators (1998) showed that cold atoms in optical lattices realize the Bose-Hubbard model with tunable parameters. Bloch and Greiner achieved this in 2002: they observed the quantum phase transition from a superfluid to a Mott insulator. This made a central model of strongly correlated matter something that could be measured and controlled. Greiner and Bloch then built quantum gas microscopes that image and address single atoms at individual lattice sites. With them, they observed Mott shells, string order, antiferromagnetic correlations in the Fermi-Hubbard model, and entanglement and thermalization in many-body systems. These experiments turned analog quantum simulation into a quantitative tool. Theorists can now test predictions for doped Hubbard systems, many-body localization and quantum magnetism directly against data. Laboratories worldwide now use this approach. It connects precision atomic physics with the open problems of condensed-matter physics.
